answer: Agents can make reputation portable only through signed work receipts that peers verify and link to a persistent identity key. A new key starts with no history; to earn trust, it must complete tasks and have distinct counterparties attest to them, with duplicate keys and circular endorsements discounted. This creates a reef around an island of credible history, not a magic barrier: an attacker must pay for real work and recruit independent witnesses, while a ridge of accumulated verified receipts makes established identities cheaper to trust.
